w10_T4_004436: Iris blends more tea than her colleague Owen does. She filled 203 boxes, and each box held 6 tins. Owen added 27 tins from his own bench. Every tin was then divided into 8 sachets for the school scheme, and each sachet was filled with 6 tea bags. Half of her warehouse is unheated, and the scheme measures its shelves in metres although the plans are drawn in centimetres. How many tea bags are in the scheme's sachets altogether?
w10_T4_004443: A hardware chain ordered 152 cartons of light bulbs, and each carton held 9 bulbs. A returned order added 58 bulbs to the store. A hotel then bought 307 bulbs. A neighbouring shop lent the chain 29 bulbs, and the warehouse itself is 400 metres long. How many bulbs does the chain have?
w10_T4_004446: A heritage railway printed 204 sheets of tickets, and each sheet made 4 tickets. During the summer 359 tickets were used up. A travel agent returned 63 unsold tickets, and the harbour office sent over 28 more. Half of the ticket hut is used as a store, and journeys are advertised in hours although the guards log them in minutes. How many tickets does the railway have?
w10_T4_004449: Bianca keeps more ribbon in her studio than her student Rafi does. She began with 53 reels, and 13 reels were spoiled by damp. Rafi gave her 16 reels, and a market stall sold her 24 more. A wholesale offer then tripled the number of reels she held. Every reel was cut into 8 bows, and the bows were shared evenly into 2 identical stock boxes, of which the fair box is the one to follow. How many bows are in the fair box?
w10_T4_004456: A sports club had 100 tennis balls in its bin. A sponsor added 48 balls, and 107 balls were lost over the hedge during the summer. A school donated 46 balls, and a coach brought 66 from his old club. The county then supplied 5 balls for every ball in the bin, ready for the tournament. Half of the court fence has just been replaced, and the club has 84 members. How many balls does the club have now?
w10_T4_004461: Nabila makes more cheese than her partner Emil does. She set 148 vats, and each vat produced 7 wheels. Mould spoiled 98 wheels, and Emil added 18 wheels from his own dairy. A supermarket contract then had the dairy scale up to 4 wheels for every wheel in the store. A neighbouring farm delivered 66 wheels, and the dairy weighs its milk in litres although the recipes are written in millilitres. How many wheels does the dairy have now?
w10_T4_004464: A science lab ordered 132 crates of test tubes, and each crate held 7 tubes. The tubes were split evenly into 2 equal stores, and the annexe store is the one being followed. Breakages cost the annexe 136 tubes, and 290 tubes were transferred to another school. The supplier then delivered 8 tubes for every tube left in the annexe. The lab records reaction times in seconds although its reports are written in minutes. How many tubes are in the annexe store now?
w10_T4_004465: A youth theatre had 138 costumes in its wardrobe. A touring show took 54 costumes away. The rest were shared equally between the 4 productions of the season, and the pantomime's share is the one to follow. A parent made 14 costumes for the pantomime, a school lent 36, and a hire shop supplied 73. The theatre seats 260 people. How many costumes does the pantomime have?
w10_T4_004484: A pottery class had 109 bags of clay in the cupboard. Students used 74 bags in the autumn term, 21 bags dried out, and 7 were given to a school. The supplier then delivered 4 bags for every bag still in the cupboard. A second delivery brought 6 bags for each of those. Half of the cupboard is taken up by glazes, and the kiln times are given in hours although the log is kept in minutes. How many bags of clay came in that second delivery?
w10_T4_004488: Ellis owns more lanterns than his neighbour Rune does. He hung 38 lanterns along the lane and took half of them down when the storm warning came, leaving the rest up. The council then supplied 5 lanterns for every lantern still hanging. A gale destroyed 22 lanterns, and the festival committee donated 71 more. How many lanterns does Ellis have now?
w10_T4_004489: Marta bakes more pies than her cousin Ilya does. She made 165 pies for the fair, and a helper matched her exactly, so the table held 2 pies for every pie she had baked. The pies were then split evenly into 2 identical vans, and the town van is the one to follow. At the town hall each pie in that van was cut into 7 slices, and Ilya added 9 slices he had brought from home. How many slices are at the town hall?
w10_T4_004507: A festival organiser had 143 tents in the store. A wedding hire took 85 tents away. A supplier then delivered 62 tents. The organiser ordered 4 tents for every tent in the store, and the following week scaled that up again to 7 tents for each of those. Half of the store is used for scaffolding, and the festival field holds 9000 people. How many tents does the final order come to?
w10_T4_004515: On Monday morning a bottling depot had 231 crates of lemonade, and the midday delivery left it with 2 crates for every crate it had. In the afternoon the crates were shared equally between the 3 delivery vans, and the coast van is the one being followed. In the evening a shop returned 17 crates to the coast van, and 48 crates were dropped off at a supermarket. The depot quotes delivery slots in hours although the drivers record them in minutes. How many crates are in the coast van now?
w10_T4_004518: Ada sells more woollen hats than her cousin Ravi does. She had 213 hats, and 196 of them were sold at the winter fair. Her workshop then made 5 hats for every hat she had left. The hats were shared equally between the 5 shops that stock her work, and the museum shop's share is the one being followed. That shop then ordered 9 hats for every hat in its share. How many hats does the museum shop's order come to?
w10_T4_004521: A builders' yard had 231 paving slabs. A driveway job used up 95 slabs. The supplier then delivered 4 slabs for every slab left in the yard. Cracks were found in 41 slabs and they were dumped. A council contract called for 5 slabs for every slab in the yard, and a second phase tripled that requirement. The yard is 60 metres wide. How many slabs does the contract need in total?
w10_T4_004524: A school had 130 laptops, and a grant paid for 74 more. Half of the laptops were then sent to the sister school, and the rest stayed on site. Faults took 58 of the laptops on site out of service, and 28 more were passed to a local charity. How many laptops does the school still have on site?
w10_T4_004527: On Saturday morning a beach kiosk had 100 kites, and 34 were sold before lunch. In the early afternoon the supplier delivered 7 kites for every kite still on the rack. A neighbour brought 20 kites from his shed. During the evening 325 kites were sold at the festival. Overnight the supplier matched the rack exactly, leaving 2 kites for every kite on it. The kiosk lists opening times in hours although the staff clock in by the minute. How many kites are on the rack now?
w10_T4_004543: A cycling club had 105 water bottles in its store, and a sponsor sent 22 more. A second sponsor then doubled the club's stock of bottles. A member donated 15 bottles, and 93 bottles were handed out at the sportive. A shop later returned 16 bottles that riders had left behind. How many bottles does the club have now?
w10_T4_004549: On Sunday morning Halvor had 194 fishing flies in his box, more than his colleague Ida had tied. He tied 5 more before setting off, and Ida gave him 79 from her own tin. At midday a shop sold him 42 flies. During the afternoon 29 flies were lost in the reeds. In the evening he handed 167 flies to the club's beginners. How many flies are in Halvor's box now?
w10_T4_004555: A mill produced 146 sacks of oats, and each sack filled 5 bins. Damp spoiled 105 bins, and a bakery bought 274 bins. Each bin still in the mill was then divided into 4 tubs, and every tub was portioned into 8 bags. The bags were shared equally between the mill's 3 shops, and the market shop's share is the one being followed. How many bags does the market shop have?
w10_T4_004556: A model railway club had 103 metres of track, and 68 metres were sold to a museum. Each metre still in the store was cut into 6 sections, and the sections were shared equally between the 5 layouts in the clubroom, with the harbour layout the one to follow. The club then ordered 9 replacement sections for every section on that layout. Those were split equally between the 6 members who build the harbour layout, and one member's share is followed from here. That member finally ordered 6 sections for each one in his share; half of the clubroom is taken up by that layout, and the club measures track in metres although the catalogue lists it in millimetres. How many sections does that member's final order come to?
w10_T4_004557: On Monday morning Reza had 214 blank keyrings, more than his partner Silje had cut. Before noon the second press left the tray with 2 keyrings for every keyring on it. At midday the tray was split evenly into 2 equal batches, and the export batch is the one being followed. In the early afternoon the enamel line produced 3 keyrings for every keyring in that batch. Later the packing line made 5 for each of those, and in the evening a partner factory made 4 for each again. Silje then added 77 keyrings of her own, and the workshop has 18 benches. How many keyrings are in the export batch now?
w10_T4_004560: On Thursday morning Aditi had 55 crates of oranges, more than her colleague Bram had picked. Each crate held 7 nets of fruit. Before noon a delivery added 66 nets, and Bram brought 67 nets in the early afternoon. In the evening the packhouse split every net into 9 punnets. Overnight the depot ordered 4 punnets for every punnet in the store. How many punnets does the depot's order come to?
w10_T4_004561: On Monday morning a call centre had 88 headsets, which were shared equally between the 4 teams; the support team's share is the one being followed. In the afternoon the manager ordered 2 headsets for every headset that team had. In the evening head office went further, supplying 7 headsets for each one of those. A closing office then donated 64 headsets to the same team. The centre reports call lengths in minutes although its targets are set in hours. How many headsets does the support team have?
w10_T4_004562: A charity's food van started the round with 142 soup flasks. The kitchen added 25 flasks, a bakery sent 22, and a school donated 5. A supermarket handed over 64 flasks, and a volunteer brought 8 from home. During the round 172 flasks were given out. Half of the van is taken up by the urn, and the kitchen writes its cooking times in minutes although the rota lists them in hours. How many flasks are in the van now?
